data.cultural_impact: The name 'Prithvina' is deeply rooted in Hindu culture, paying homage to the divine goddess of the earth, Prithvi. It carries the meaning of 'one who belongs to the earth' or 'daughter of the earth'. Thus, this name promotes a connection with nature and reverence for the earth and its abundant resources.
data.spiritual_significance: 'Prithvina' embodies the spiritual essence of groundedness, stability, and the cyclical nature of creation and destruction. It signifies an individual's connection to the Earth as the source of life and nurturing force. By adopting this name, one can seek the blessings of Prithvi Devi to lead a life in harmony with nature and the divine energies that sustain it.

historical_references.reference: Prithiviraj Chauhan, also known as Prithvi Raj III, was a Hindu ruler of the Chauhan dynasty in the 12th century. He is best known for his resistance against the invading Muslim armies led by Muhammad Ghori.

Prithvi Narayan Sahu II was a king of the Sahu dynasty of Odisha, who ruled from 1793 to 1811. He is known for his efforts to expand the kingdom and strengthen its defenses, as well as his patronage of art and culture.
